doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Circuses and parades draw him to the drums
summary: The circus grounds in front of the house and the drum sections of parades captivated him and he wanted no other instrument.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: You know you gotta’ start some place and you know I was helped along and encouraged by watching circuses when they come to town we lived on one side the street and in front of our house were the circus grounds so that was a lot of fun seeing them unload the cars, and to see elephants pushing trucks and stuff like that
You say you were influenced by the music of the circus?
Oh yeah we went to the show. It was one of the managers—he’d come early in the morning and he’d come and my mom would make a big hot pot of coffee and give it to him.
What was it about the music that was so captivating for you.

Well mainly it was the drums that captivated me,. To see a parade and the whole, the whole center, the main portion of the parade, was the drum section. Cause everybody was marching and just to listen to that and see the discipline was formed in that way—that was fascinating to me.
So you’re saying that the first instrument you were attracted to was the drums even though your brothers played other instruments?
I didn’t want to do anything else
